rules.statement: In a PowerShell double-quoted string, write a variable that is immediately followed by literal text such as `[`, `:` or a name character with braces (`"${name}[bot]"`), not bare (`"$name[bot]"`).
rules.why: `"$login[bot]"` does expand correctly, but readers take it for indexing, so the braced form makes the intent clear.
rules.check: Look for double-quoted PowerShell strings where `$var` is directly followed by `[`, `:` or similar text without `${...}` delimiting.

rules.statement: When a test stand-in or parser accepts several syntactic forms of the same input (for example `-X GET`, `-XGET`, `--method=GET`), have at least one check for each form the change claims to support, written so that breaking that form's handling makes the check fail.
rules.why: A form with no check of its own can regress while CI still passes, and the PR description then claims more coverage than the tests give.
rules.check: Compare the forms the PR description or code says are handled with the test checks, and flag any form that no check exercises.

rules.statement: Move the same lookup expression, when it is written out in several places, into one helper and call that helper from each place.
rules.why: A later fix to one copy, such as its not-found handling, may not reach the others.
rules.check: Look for the same non-trivial lookup or query expression pasted into several route blocks or functions in a diff.

rules.statement: Don't flag a dated `## [<version>] - <date>` CHANGELOG section added in a pull request as breaking the `[Unreleased]` rule when the pull request's plan has a `Release:` line. Such a plan writes its version's section in its last step, leaves `[Unreleased]` empty and points the `[unreleased]` compare link at the new tag.
rules.why: The `[Unreleased]` rule applies only to plans without a `Release:` line. Release plans are tagged and published from the dated section after the merge, so the compare links resolve.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the plan has a `Release:` line, read the plan skills' changelog rule, and see whether earlier versions were released the same way.
